board.name: other-m68k
board.desc: 68000 SBC: 1 MB SRAM, 1 MB flash ROM window (128 KB BIOS image), memory-mapped 320x240x8 composite colour framebuffer that time-slices the SRAM with the CPU, PS/2 keyboard, bit-banged SD, 68681 DUART serial, 8-bit PDM audio (one byte per video line shifted out by CPLD2).

memory_map.name: RAM
memory_map.desc: 1 MB SRAM. Time-sliced with the video fetch; CPU accesses are phase-aligned by DTACK (0 or 2 wait clocks). CPLD1 drives MA0..MA16 (CPU A1..A17 or the video counter); CPLD2 drives MA17..MA18 (CPU A18..A19 in the CPU half of a slot, the framebuffer pages' fixed bits 19..18 during the video fetch). At reset the ROM is overlaid here until the first access to the ROM region.

memory_map.name: ROM
memory_map.device: 2x SST39SF040-70 (512Kx8 NOR flash, 70 ns, 5 V), word wide, CE tied low
memory_map.desc: 1 MB flash window; the BIOS image occupies the first 128 KB (ROM_IMAGE_SIZE, checksum in its last word), the rest is free (erased 0xFF). Reads: zero wait states, not subject to slot alignment. Writes get DTACK and reach the chips (ROMWE), so the firmware can reprogram itself in place with the JEDEC command sequence (see "flash"). Vectors at offset 0 (overlaid at 0x000000 at reset).

memory_map.name: IO
memory_map.desc: CPLD2 peripheral registers. 16-bit word access only; address bits A4..A15 are not decoded, so the 16-byte register block repeats through the region. INTEN, GPIO and AUDIO are write-only (read as 0): the fitter budget does not allow read-back; software keeps shadows. SDIO reads back the six card lines.

memory_map.name: SWITCHES
memory_map.desc: CPLD1 soft switches. Write-only; writing any value to the address performs the action. Reads return garbage.

memory_map.name: DUART
memory_map.device: MC68681 / SCN68681 / SCC68681 DUART, 3.6864 MHz crystal
memory_map.desc: 68681 DUART. Byte registers on D7..D0 at ODD addresses (A1..A4 -> RS1..RS4); A5..A15 ignored. Use odd-address byte accesses only: an even-byte or word cycle still selects the chip (undefined data; a read pops the FIFO into the wrong lane). DTACK comes from the DUART (open drain, shared with CPLD1); accesses are not slot aligned.

unmapped_policy: BERR asserted (bus error exception) for any access outside the regions above, except the interrupt-acknowledge pattern A23..A4 all ones, which is autovectored via VPA.

flash.device: SST39SF040-70-4C-PHE, one per byte lane (U4 = D15..D8 even bytes, U5 = D7..D0 odd bytes)
flash.desc: Both chips see the same command sequence because every command is issued as a WORD write with the byte repeated in both halves: chip byte address N is CPU address ROM_BASE + 2N, so the JEDEC unlock addresses 0x5555/0x2AAA become FLASH_CMD1 = ROM_BASE + 0xAAAA and FLASH_CMD2 = ROM_BASE + 0x5554. Program a word: 0xAAAA->CMD1, 0x5555->CMD2, 0xA0A0->CMD1, data->address, then poll until a read returns the data (each byte shows toggling DQ6 / inverted DQ7 while busy; at most 20 us). Erase the 8 KB (CPU view) sector holding address X: 0xAAAA->CMD1, 0x5555->CMD2, 0x8080->CMD1, 0xAAAA->CMD1, 0x5555->CMD2, 0x3030->X, poll until 0xFFFF (at most 25 ms). ID: 0xAAAA->CMD1, 0x5555->CMD2, 0x9090->CMD1; read ROM_BASE -> 0xBFBF, ROM_BASE+2 -> 0xB7B7; 0xF0F0 anywhere exits. Programming only clears bits: erase first. The chips cannot be read (code cannot run from them) while an operation is in progress, so the routine that issues commands runs from RAM with interrupts masked; the NMI button must not be pressed meanwhile. Only word writes are used; a byte write would present the same byte to both chips (the 68000 duplicates write data on both bus halves) and is not part of the protocol.

ram_layout.name: VECTORS
ram_layout.desc: Exception vector table (RAM after overlay clears).

ram_layout.name: SYSDATA
ram_layout.desc: BIOS .data/.bss; supervisor stack grows down from the top (0x004000).

ram_layout.name: USER
ram_layout.desc: User program load region (ELF link address 0x004000). User stack grows down from the top (0x0DA800). Extends to 0x0ED400 if page 1 of the framebuffer is not used.

video.pixel_desc: bits 7..5 red, 4..2 green, 1..0 blue. Byte at the even (upper, D15..D8) address is the left pixel of the word.
video.encoder: AD724 (RGB in, composite out). Standard (NTSC/PAL) fixed by two pull resistors (STND, PALJMP) plus the matching subcarrier crystal; the CPLD timing table is selected by soft switch; jumper state readable in INTSTAT.PALJMP.

ntsc.desc: 12 MHz CPU clocks per line; 191 slots of 4 clocks. 15.707 kHz / 59.95 Hz, non-interlaced ('240p').

pal.desc: 192 slots of 4 clocks. 15.625 kHz / 50.08 Hz, non-interlaced; 240 active lines letterboxed.

video.line_origin: Horizontal count 0 = first active pixel; vertical count 0 = first active line. The VBLANK interrupt flag sets at the leading edge of vertical sync (line v_active + v_bottom), not at the end of active video.
video.timing_note: All horizontal quantities are CPU clocks and are multiples of the 4-clock slot, so the active region never jitters against the slot grid. Video fetches one 16-bit word (two pixels) per slot during the active region.

regs.name: INTSTAT
regs.desc: Interrupt and pin status. Reading returns flags and live pin levels; bits not listed read 0. Writing 1 to a clearable bit clears it.

fields.name: VBLANK
fields.desc: Set at the leading edge of vertical sync (3 lines after the last active line on NTSC). W1C.

fields.name: HSYNC
fields.desc: Set at start of each horizontal sync. W1C.

fields.name: PS2RDY
fields.desc: PS/2 byte received; cleared by reading PS2DATA.

fields.name: DUARTIRQ
fields.desc: Live level of the DUART IRQ pin, inverted (1 = DUART requesting). Read the DUART ISR for the cause.

fields.name: PS2ERR
fields.desc: PS/2 framing/parity error on last byte. W1C.

fields.name: NMIBTN
fields.desc: Live level of the NMI/break pushbutton (1 = pressed).

fields.name: PS2CLK
fields.desc: Live level of PS/2 clock line.

fields.name: PS2DAT
fields.desc: Live level of PS/2 data line.

fields.name: PALJMP
fields.desc: 1 = board built for PAL (PALJMP pulled high); rev B pulls it low (NTSC).

fields.name: VSYNCPIN
fields.desc: Live vertical sync (1 during vsync lines).

fields.name: DEPIN
fields.desc: Live display enable (1 during active video).

regs.name: INTEN
regs.desc: Interrupt enables (write-only, reads 0). A pending flag with its enable set drives IPL at the level listed in interrupts[].

fields.name: VBLANK
fields.desc: Enable level-1 interrupt on VBLANK flag.

fields.name: HSYNC
fields.desc: Enable level-4 interrupt on HSYNC flag.

fields.name: DUART
fields.desc: Enable level-3 interrupt while the DUART IRQ pin is asserted.

regs.name: SDIO
regs.desc: SD card lines, native 4-bit SD bus bit-banged by the CPU (revision 7). Each bit is an open-drain driver: writing 0 drives the line low, writing 1 releases it to the 10 k pull-up (3.3 V). Reading returns the LEVEL of each line in the same bit position (the card drives CMD during responses and DAT0..3 during reads), so no shadow is needed: read-modify-write works, but the usual loop writes a precomputed word per clock phase. The card samples CMD/DAT on the rising edge of CLK and drives them after the falling edge; the CPU drives CLK low (bit 1 = 0), sets CMD/DAT, then releases CLK (bit 1 = 1). Reset 0x003F: everything released, bus idle with CLK high. SPI mode is no longer wired: CMD has no divider and the card's responses come back on CMD.

fields.name: DAT3
fields.desc: DAT3 (the SPI-mode CS pin). Data line in 4-bit mode; drive low = 0, release = 1.

fields.name: CLK
fields.desc: Card clock, host driven: 0 drives low, 1 releases high. Idle high.

fields.name: CMD
fields.desc: Command line, bidirectional: host commands (with CRC7), card responses.

fields.name: DAT0
fields.desc: Data line 0 (the only data line in 1-bit mode; busy signal after a write).

regs.name: GPIO
regs.desc: Misc outputs (write-only, reads 0). PS/2 lines are open-drain: 1 releases the line (read it via INTSTAT), 0 pulls it low. Bit 2 is unused since revision 5 (audio moved to the AUDIO register) and must be written 0.

regs.name: PS2DATA
regs.desc: Last PS/2 byte received (bits 7..0). Reading clears INTSTAT.PS2RDY.

regs.name: AUDIO
regs.desc: PDM audio shifter (write-only, reads 0). The low byte is loaded into an 8-bit rotating shift register whose bit 7 drives the audio pin. CPLD2 rotates it left one place at the leading edge of HSYNC and then every 24 bus slots (192 CLK24 cycles = 96 CPU clocks), i.e. 8 bits per video line, bit 7 first, ~126 kHz PDM; the rotation is resynchronised to HSYNC so it never drifts. Because the register rotates rather than shifting in zeros, a line without a write repeats the previous byte. Write once per line from the HSYNC interrupt, as early in the line as possible; the write replaces the register immediately. The bit pattern is a pulse-density code: the fraction of 1 bits sets the output level (0x00 silence/low, 0xAA or 0x55 mid-level, 0xFF high). The BIOS encodes 8-bit unsigned samples into patterns with a first-order sigma-delta table (the SDK's pdm_encode; the BIOS streams them with audio_start/audio_next/audio_last); a program may also write patterns directly. Writing 0x00 or 0xFF for whole lines and toggling between them gives the old 1-bit behaviour.

fields.name: PATTERN
fields.desc: PDM bit pattern, bit 7 is shifted out first.

regs.name: ID
regs.desc: Board/glue identification: 0x68 in the upper byte, CPLD2 logic revision in the lower byte (2 = DUART board).

io.desc: CPLD2 peripheral registers. 16-bit word access only; address bits A4..A15 are not decoded, so the 16-byte register block repeats through the region. INTEN, GPIO and AUDIO are write-only (read as 0): the fitter budget does not allow read-back; software keeps shadows. SDIO reads back the six card lines.

regs.name: PAGE0
regs.desc: Display framebuffer page 0 (0x0ED400) starting next frame.

regs.name: PAGE1
regs.desc: Display framebuffer page 1 (0x0DA800) starting next frame.

regs.name: NTSC
regs.desc: Select NTSC (262-line) timing table. Default at reset.

regs.name: PAL
regs.desc: Select PAL (312-line) timing table.

duart.desc: MC68681 registers; one name per direction where read and write differ at the same offset. Offsets 5 and 21 must not be READ (factory test locations: CRA/CRB are write-only). Even-address bytes and word accesses in this region do hit the chip (DUARTCS is asserted for any cycle in the region) with undefined data: do not use them.

regs.name: MRA
regs.desc: Mode register: first access after reset or a 'reset MR pointer' command is MR1 (bits: 1..0 bits per char 00=5..11=8, 2 parity mode, 4..3 parity type, 5 error mode, 6 RX interrupt select, 7 RX RTS control), the next is MR2 (bits: 3..0 stop bits (0x7 = 1 stop), 4 CTS enable TX, 5 RTS control, 7..6 channel mode 00 = normal).

regs.name: SRA
regs.desc: Status register A.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.desc: Receiver ready: a character is in the FIFO.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.desc: Transmitter ready to accept a character.

fields.name: PE
fields.desc: Parity error (of the character at the FIFO top).

regs.name: CSRA
regs.desc: Clock select: bits 7..4 receiver, 3..0 transmitter baud code from the data-sheet table (set 1, ACR[7]=0: 0xC = 38.4k, 0xB = 9600, 0x8 = 2400; set 2 swaps some rows, e.g. 0xC = 19.2k).

regs.name: CRA
regs.desc: Command register: bits 1..0 RX enable/disable (01 enable, 10 disable), 3..2 TX enable/disable, 7..4 misc command (0001 reset MR pointer, 0010 reset RX, 0011 reset TX, 0100 reset error status, 0101 reset break-change interrupt).

regs.name: RBA
regs.desc: Receiver buffer A (FIFO top); reading pops the FIFO.

regs.name: TBA
regs.desc: Transmitter buffer A.

regs.name: IPCR
regs.desc: Input port change register.

regs.name: ACR
regs.desc: Auxiliary control: bit 7 baud-rate set (0 = set 1, used here: 0xC = 38.4k), bits 6..4 counter/timer mode and source, bits 3..0 IP change interrupt enables.

regs.name: ISR
regs.desc: Interrupt status register.

regs.name: IMR
regs.desc: Interrupt mask register (same bits as ISR).

regs.name: CUR
regs.desc: Counter upper byte.

regs.name: CTUR
regs.desc: Counter/timer upper preset.

regs.name: CLR
regs.desc: Counter lower byte.

regs.name: CTLR
regs.desc: Counter/timer lower preset.

regs.name: MRB
regs.desc: Mode register: first access after reset or a 'reset MR pointer' command is MR1B (bits: 1..0 bits per char 00=5..11=8, 2 parity mode, 4..3 parity type, 5 error mode, 6 RX interrupt select, 7 RX RTS control), the next is MR2B (bits: 3..0 stop bits (0x7 = 1 stop), 4 CTS enable TX, 5 RTS control, 7..6 channel mode 00 = normal).

regs.name: SRB
regs.desc: Status register B.

fields.name: RXRDY
fields.desc: Receiver ready: a character is in the FIFO.

fields.name: TXRDY
fields.desc: Transmitter ready to accept a character.

fields.name: PE
fields.desc: Parity error (of the character at the FIFO top).

regs.name: CSRB
regs.desc: Clock select: bits 7..4 receiver, 3..0 transmitter baud code from the data-sheet table (set 1, ACR[7]=0: 0xC = 38.4k, 0xB = 9600, 0x8 = 2400; set 2 swaps some rows, e.g. 0xC = 19.2k).

regs.name: CRB
regs.desc: Command register: bits 1..0 RX enable/disable (01 enable, 10 disable), 3..2 TX enable/disable, 7..4 misc command (0001 reset MR pointer, 0010 reset RX, 0011 reset TX, 0100 reset error status, 0101 reset break-change interrupt).

regs.name: RBB
regs.desc: Receiver buffer B.

regs.name: TBB
regs.desc: Transmitter buffer B.

regs.name: IVR
regs.desc: Interrupt vector register. Unused: IACK is tied high and interrupts are autovectored.

regs.name: IP
regs.desc: Input port IP0..IP6 (unlatched).

regs.name: OPCR
regs.desc: Output port configuration register.

regs.name: START_CTR
regs.desc: Address-triggered command: start counter/timer.

regs.name: OPR_SET
regs.desc: Output port register: set the bits written as 1.

regs.name: STOP_CTR
regs.desc: Address-triggered command: stop counter/timer.

regs.name: OPR_RESET
regs.desc: Output port register: clear the bits written as 1.

interrupts.name: VBLANK
interrupts.desc: Leading edge of vertical sync, ~60 Hz (NTSC) / 50 Hz (PAL).

interrupts.name: DUART
interrupts.desc: 68681 interrupt (receiver ready, transmitter ready, counter/timer, ...): read the DUART ISR. Level sensitive; the DUART IACK pin is tied high, so this is autovectored like the others.

interrupts.name: HSYNC
interrupts.desc: Line tick, 15.7 kHz; audio sample timer.

interrupts.name: NMI
interrupts.desc: Break into monitor. Edge-triggered by the 68000.

interrupt_mode: autovector (VPA asserted by CPLD1 on every IACK; the DUART's IACK pin is tied inactive); vector = 24 + level

serial.device: MC68681 DUART channel A (channel B TXD/RXD brought to the expansion header)
serial.init: MR1A=0x13 (8 bits, no parity), MR2A=0x07 (1 stop), ACR=0x00 (baud-rate set 1), CSRA=0xCC (38.4k RX and TX), CRA=0x05 (enable RX+TX); IMR bit 1 (RXRDYA) for receive interrupts
serial.note: 38400 is the highest rate in the 68681's fixed tables: CSR code 0xC is 38.4k in set 1 (ACR[7]=0) and 19.2k in set 2 (ACR[7]=1), data sheet Table 4-5. The counter/timer or an external 16x clock could give more but are not used.
serial.connector: 6-pin FTDI header (GND, CTS, VCC, TXD, RXD, RTS); 5V TTL levels, FT232H inputs are 5V tolerant; CTS/RTS not connected

ps2.rx: hardware 11-bit frame receiver in CPLD2 (start, 8 data, odd parity, stop) -> PS2DATA + PS2RDY
ps2.tx: software bit-bang via GPIO.PS2CLK/PS2DAT open-drain bits

sd.mode: Native SD bus (not SPI), 4-bit data, bit-banged through SDIO. All six lines (CLK, CMD, DAT0..3) are open-drain from the 5 V CPLD2 with 10 k pull-ups to 3.3 V; the CPU drives a line low or releases it and reads every line back from SDIO. Commands carry CRC7 (48-bit frames on CMD, responses R1/R2/R3/R6/R7 read back on CMD). Data blocks are 512 bytes sent as 1024 nibbles on DAT3..0 (MSB nibble first), start bit (all four lines low), then 16 CRC16-CCITT bits per line, end bit; the BIOS ignores the CRC on reads and computes the four CRC16s on writes. Initialisation: 74+ clocks, CMD0, CMD8 (SDHC), ACMD41 until ready (HCS set), CMD2 (CID), CMD3 (RCA), CMD7 (select), ACMD6 (4-bit bus), CMD16 512 (SDSC); block I/O with CMD17 / CMD24 (single block), busy on DAT0 after a write. Speed: two clock pulses per byte of data (a nibble per pulse) instead of eight in SPI mode.
sd.power: 3.3V LDO; CLK, CMD, DAT0..3 open-drain from CPLD2 (drive low / release) with 10 k pull-ups to 3.3 V; no level dividers.
sd.filesystem: FAT12/16/32 via FatFs (LFN off). A FAT32 volume needs >= 65525 clusters: use cards/images of 64 MB or more for FAT32 (smaller ones are FAT16, also fine).

audio.desc: AUDIO register -> 8-bit rotating PDM shifter in CPLD2 (8 bits per video line, ~126 kHz) -> 1 k / 10 nF RC low-pass -> 10 k : 2.2 k divider -> 10 uF DC-blocking cap -> 3.5mm jack. Sampled audio: the program hands the BIOS buffers of PDM pattern bytes (audio_start / audio_next / audio_last, AUDIO_NBUF buffers of up to AUDIO_BUF_MAX bytes, producer/consumer, optionally blocking so the program is paced to the line rate); the BIOS HSYNC interrupt writes one byte per line (15.7 kHz NTSC, 15.6 kHz PAL) and does no other per-sample work. Encoding 8-bit unsigned samples (128 = silence) into patterns is the program's job, normally through the SDK's pdm_init/pdm_encode (first-order sigma-delta, 8-bit accumulator x 7-bit sample table built in RAM). The pattern of a line is repeated by the hardware if no new byte arrives. Beeps: write 0x00/0xFF patterns at the tone rate. Idle level: the mid pattern 0xAA (50 % density) so starting and stopping playback does not click.

reset.supervisor: open-drain voltage supervisor + pushbutton -> SYSRESET; diodes to 68000 RESET and HALT; SYSRESET also resets both CPLDs. The RESET instruction does not reset the glue (so the ROM overlay is not re-armed by software).

syscall.desc: TRAP #15 with the call number in D0.W. Integer args in D1..D3, pointer args in A0..A1 in the order listed. Result in D0.L. All other registers preserved.

syscalls.name: exit
syscalls.desc: Terminate the program and return to the monitor.

syscalls.name: putchar
syscalls.desc: Write a character to the console (video + serial).

syscalls.name: getchar
syscalls.desc: Blocking read of one character from keyboard or serial.

syscalls.name: pollchar
syscalls.desc: Non-blocking read; -1 if no character is available.

syscalls.name: puts
syscalls.desc: Write a NUL-terminated string to the console (no newline added).

syscalls.name: serial_putc
syscalls.desc: Write a byte to the serial port only.

syscalls.name: serial_getc
syscalls.desc: Non-blocking serial read; -1 if none.

syscalls.name: ticks
syscalls.desc: Frames since boot (VBLANK counter, ~60 Hz).

syscalls.name: wait_vblank
syscalls.desc: Block until the next vertical blanking interval.

syscalls.name: video_info
syscalls.desc: Fill in framebuffer geometry, page addresses and current page.

syscalls.name: video_set_page
syscalls.desc: Select displayed framebuffer page (0 or 1); takes effect at next frame.

syscalls.name: open
syscalls.desc: Open a file on the SD card (8.3 names, O_* flags from the ABI; O_CREAT/O_TRUNC/O_APPEND values differ from newlib's, the SDK shim translates). Returns fd >= 3 or a negative error; fds 0..2 are the console.

syscalls.name: close
syscalls.desc: Close a file.

syscalls.name: read
syscalls.desc: Read up to len bytes. Returns count or negative error.

syscalls.name: write
syscalls.desc: Write len bytes. Returns count or negative error.

syscalls.name: lseek
syscalls.desc: Reposition; returns new offset or negative error.

syscalls.name: opendir
syscalls.desc: Open a directory; returns handle or negative error.

syscalls.name: readdir
syscalls.desc: Next entry; 1 if filled, 0 at end, negative error.

syscalls.name: closedir
syscalls.desc: Close a directory handle.

syscalls.name: sd_read_block
syscalls.desc: Raw 512-byte block read.

syscalls.name: sd_write_block
syscalls.desc: Raw 512-byte block write.

syscalls.name: set_irq_handler
syscalls.desc: Install a user interrupt handler for level 1..4 (called from the BIOS ISR in supervisor mode at that interrupt's own priority, so higher levels can still interrupt it); returns the previous one. NULL restores default.

syscalls.name: mem_info
syscalls.desc: Report the user RAM region available to the program.

syscalls.name: con_set_cursor
syscalls.desc: Move the console text cursor.

syscalls.name: con_clear
syscalls.desc: Clear the console.

syscalls.name: con_info
syscalls.desc: Console columns, rows, cursor position.

syscalls.name: exec
syscalls.desc: Load and run another ELF executable from the SD card with argument string `args`. Returns a negative error only if the file cannot be opened or does not fit user RAM, before any user memory is overwritten; otherwise the new program replaces the caller and its exit returns to the monitor.

syscalls.name: key_event
syscalls.desc: Next raw keyboard event: bit 8 = release, bits 7..0 = PS/2 set-2 scan code (E0-prefixed codes have bit 9 set); -1 if none.

syscalls.name: sleep_ms
syscalls.desc: Delay for approximately ms milliseconds.

syscalls.name: set_audio_cb
syscalls.desc: Install a function called from the HSYNC interrupt once per video line (15.7 kHz NTSC) in supervisor mode; it takes over the AUDIO register (the buffer stream of audio_start/next/last is not serviced while a callback is installed, and audio_start fails while one is) and should write one PDM pattern per call. NULL disables.

syscalls.name: audio_start
syscalls.desc: Begin streaming PDM pattern bytes to the AUDIO register, one byte per video line (15.7 kHz NTSC, 15.6 kHz PAL). The BIOS owns AUDIO_NBUF buffers of AUDIO_BUF_MAX bytes; bufsize (1..AUDIO_BUF_MAX) is how many bytes of each the program will fill and the hardware will play. Resets the stream (anything queued is dropped, the output goes to the idle pattern) and returns the first buffer to fill. Non-blocking. Returns NULL if bufsize is out of range or an audio callback is installed. The bytes are raw hardware patterns: encode samples with the SDK's pdm_encode (first-order sigma-delta) or write patterns directly. Playback starts at the first audio_next.

syscalls.name: audio_next
syscalls.desc: Hand the BIOS a buffer the program has filled (one obtained from audio_start or a previous audio_next) and get the next buffer to fill. Buffers play in the order handed in; the HSYNC interrupt is enabled while any are queued. If no buffer is free: block != 0 waits (interrupts enabled) until the one being played finishes, which paces the program to the audio rate; block == 0 returns NULL at once and the program retries later (the handed buffer is still accepted). filled == NULL hands nothing in and only tries to obtain a free buffer. Returns NULL also when the stream is not started, or when filled is not one of the BIOS buffers.

syscalls.name: audio_last
syscalls.desc: Hand in the final buffer (filled may be NULL for none) and end the stream. block != 0 waits until everything queued has played; block == 0 returns at once and the queued buffers finish playing on their own. When the last byte has played the handler writes the idle pattern 0xAA and disables the HSYNC interrupt, so idle audio costs no CPU. Returns 0, or E_INVAL if the stream was not started. Exiting the program stops the stream at once instead: queued buffers are dropped, the idle pattern is written and the interrupt is disabled.

abi.desc: Structures and constants shared by BIOS, SDK and emulator. Struct fields are 32-bit (or char arrays) so layout is identical for the m68k and the host. User program entry: USP points at {return address (exit stub), argc, argv} as for a C `_start(argc, argv)`; argv[0] is the path as given to `run`/`exec`, further words split on blanks (at most 16 words, 255 bytes). The monitor's `go` enters with argc 0 and argv[0] NULL. Filenames are 8.3 (FatFs with LFN off), case-insensitive; E_NAMETOOLONG for anything else. Pointers passed to syscalls must lie in user RAM (USER_BASE..RAM_END, framebuffers included) or the call fails with E_FAULT.

cpld1.role: MMU: CPU clock divider, address decode, ROM overlay, flash read/write strobes, DTACK/BERR/VPA, SRAM address mux and strobes, video address counter, H/V timing, soft switches, DUART chip select (DTACK released during DUART cycles)

cpld2.role: I/O and shifter: video word latch and RGB332 pixel output, interrupt controller (incl. DUART IRQ), PS/2 receiver, 4-bit SD card lines (open drain, read back), GPIO bits, 8-bit PDM audio shifter, registers, upper SRAM address bits MA17..MA18 (CPU A18..A19 in the CPU half of each slot, the framebuffer page bits during the video fetch)

glue.bus_buffers: 2x 74AHCT245 between the CPU data bus (CPU, flash, DUART on D0..D7) and the SRAM-side data bus (SRAMs, CPLD2). Enabled only during the CPU half of each slot for RAM and IO cycles; direction from R/W.
glue.dtack: DTACK is an open-drain bus with a 4.7k pull-up: CPLD1 drives it low (and high again) for RAM, ROM, IO and SWITCHES cycles and releases it (high-Z) whenever AS is low in the DUART region; the DUART's open-drain DTACK answers those cycles. The DUART IRQ (open drain, pull-up) is an input of CPLD2; its IACK pin is tied high.
